title: Scaling a Circle Membership Year's Credit by the Member's Spend
content:
The figure a Northbeam Circle Membership year's credit starts from is scaled by what the member has
spent, read from the qualifying spend and the earning occasions booked on the membership in the twelve
months ending on the handling day.

## The scale

1. Where the qualifying spend booked in the twelve months ending on the handling day reaches the
   qualifying spend figure of the tier and three or more earning occasions were booked in that window, the
   figure is taken at the higher spend multiple of this schedule, 1.2.
2. Where that qualifying spend reaches the mid spend share of the qualifying spend figure of the tier —
   one half, 50 percent, of it — but not the figure itself, and two or more earning occasions were booked
   in that window, the figure is taken at the middle spend multiple of this schedule, 1.1.
3. Where neither of those holds, the figure is taken as it stands, at a multiple of 1.

## The tier figure the readings turn on

| Tier | Qualifying spend figure (USD) | One half of that figure (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| Circle Free Membership | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| Circle Plus Annual | 2500.00 | 1250.00 |
| Circle Total Annual | 9000.00 | 4500.00 |
| Circle Total Household Annual | 9000.00 | 4500.00 |
| Circle Business Pro | 40000.00 | 20000.00 |
| Circle Business Elite | 250000.00 | 125000.00 |

## Both sides of each boundary

On Circle Plus Annual, qualifying spend of 2500.00 with 3 earning occasions reaches the tier's figure and
takes the higher multiple; the same 2500.00 with 2 occasions reaches the figure but not the occasion count of
the first reading, and does not reach the second reading either, because that reading turns on the spend
falling below the tier's figure — so the figure is taken as it stands. Spend of 2499.99 with 2 occasions
takes the middle multiple; spend of 1249.99 with 2 occasions takes neither, being below one half of 2500.00.
A starting figure of 80.00 therefore stands at 96.00 under the first reading, 88.00 under the second and
80.00 under the third.
